profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
The Satyavedu Assembly Constituency, established in 1962, is located in the southern part of Tirupati District, bordering Tamil Nadu. It covers seven mandals—Narayanavanam, Pichatur, K.V.B. Puram, Nagalapuram, Satyavedu, Varadaiahpalem, and B.N. Kandriga—spanning 1,669.71 sq. km with 1.58 lakh hectares of geographical area. The region has diverse soils like red, black cotton, and gravelly soils, supporting paddy, groundnut, sugarcane, pulses, mango, watermelon, and flower crops. With water resources such as the Telugu Ganga Canal, Araniar Project, Kalangi Reservoir, and nearly 469 irrigation tanks, agriculture remains a vital part of life. Culturally, the constituency is home to significant temples like Narayanavanam Sri Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Nagalapuram Vedanarayana Swamy Temple, Pallikondeswara Swamy Temple, and many more, attracting pilgrims and tourists.


Economically, Satyavedu is a major industrial hub, led by Sri City (Satyavedu Reserve Infrastructure City), a world-class integrated business township and SEZ hosting over 180 companies from 27 countries, including Foxconn, PepsiCo, Amara Raja, Isuzu, Dixon Technologies, and Cadbury. Industry contributes 40% of the economy, while agriculture and services contribute 30% each, making it one of the most balanced growth centers in Andhra Pradesh. The constituency has a population of around 2.77 lakh, with a literacy rate of 65.66%, and growing social infrastructure including schools, colleges, PHCs, and housing projects. With strong road, rail, air, and port connectivity, along with its rich cultural heritage, Satyavedu is emerging as a dynamic region that combines agriculture, industry, services, and tourism, positioning it as a key driver of regional development.

economy_text.economy_Text:
Economy at a Glance


As of 2023–24, Satyavedu’s Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) stands at ₹15,654 crore, and is projected to more than double to ₹34,445 crore by 2028–29, growing at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 17.08%. This robust economic outlook is driven by strong performance across industry, services, and agriculture sectors.

The industrial sector is the cornerstone of Satyavedu’s economy, contributing ₹10,488 crore in 2023–24 and projected to reach ₹22,561 crore by 2028–29. Anchored by the 7,500-acre Sri City Industrial Park, this sector includes manufacturing, logistics, electronics, and food processing industries. Future growth is expected through expansion of IP Chinnapandur, MSME integration with ONDC, and positioning Sri City as a hub for IT and technology-based industries.

The service sector, valued at ₹2,247 crore, is growing steadily with a target of ₹5,075 crore by 2028–29. This growth is supported by emerging activity in logistics, retail, education, healthcare, and tourism, especially around temple towns like Narayanavanam and Nagalapuram.

The agriculture and allied sector, currently contributing ₹1,936 crore, is expected to reach ₹3,965 crore by 2029–30. Major crops include paddy, sugarcane, groundnut, and horticulture, supported by extensive irrigation infrastructure like the Telugu Ganga Canal and Kalangi Reservoir. Promotion of solar irrigation, water management, and agri-value chains will enhance productivity and sustainability.

With its industrial backbone, growing service base, and modernizing agriculture, Satyavedu is positioned to become a high-growth, multi-sectoral economic hub in southern Andhra Pradesh.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Satyavedu is experiencing rapid economic growth with a targeted 17% annual GCDP growth rate, fueled by industrial expansion, Manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, agri-value chains, and emerging service sectors. With the development of Sri City, solar energy initiatives, and IT infrastructure, the constituency is on a transformative path to become a major industrial and economic powerhouse in Andhra Pradesh by 2047.
